note: Detector-level invariants for the 25-binary adversarial type-recovery corpus. These encode GROUND-TRUTH expectations derived from each binary's C source (recovered structs/offsets, cross-function merge requirements, union-discrimination, noise bounds). They are DESIRED behavior: `scripts/run_type_test_bins.py --check` fails when the detector regresses (drops a real struct, fails a required merge, fabricates a union, or explodes candidate count). Offsets are byte offsets from the recovered base as Binja reports them; where -O0/-O2 legally differ the expectations are keyed per optimization level. Ranges are intentionally loose where register/analysis noise is inherent.

01.name: nested
01.about: struct record {inner_item* item@0; uint16 flags@8; char* label@16} shared across 3 mutually-calling functions; each sees a partial view. The cross-function merge MUST unify into one candidate.

02.name: llist
02.about: struct lnode {void* key@0; struct lnode* next@8; uint64 val@16} shared across find/insert/remove. Merge required.

03.name: pointers
03.about: struct table_entry {char* name@0; uint64 value@8}; pointer-to-pointer table. Must NOT flatten the pointer chain into garbage offsets.

04.name: union_halves
04.about: genuine union u {uint64 raw@0; struct{uint16 lo; uint32 mid;}} + struct packet{u; uint8 len@8}. Access widths differ at +0 -> overlap MUST fire (a real union).

05.name: false_merge
05.about: two unrelated structs {uint32,uint32} passed to a generic void* helper with identical offsets. Detector legitimately merges; the LLM verdict is the gate. Detector check: the merged offsets {0,4} ARE present (over-merge is the model's job to reject).

06.name: canary_noise
06.about: TLS stack canary (fsbase+0x28) + register-temp noise must be suppressed while the ONE real struct config {0,4,8,16,31} is recovered. Bounds deliberately lenient for -O2 register/`i` temp noise (the verdict rejects those); the invariant is: the real multi-offset config struct IS recovered and canary bases never appear.

07.name: false_merge_regs
07.about: two unrelated structs {0,8} reaching a common helper via registers at -O2. Over-merge tolerated at detector level (verdict gates).

08.name: union_widths
08.about: union u_state: same bytes at +0 read as int32 (4B) and uint64 (8B). Overlap hint MUST fire.

09.name: common_prefix
09.about: struct net_hdr {0,4,6} and udp_dgram {0,4,6,10} share a header. Detector merges via same pointer; verdict must NOT fabricate mixed semantics. Detector check: offsets {0,4,6,10} present.

10.name: tagged_union
10.about: variant {uint64 tag@0; union{ pair a,b @8/16 ; str len @16} payload}; union member at +8 aliased by read_pair (int64) and read_str_len (uint32 at +16). Overlap expected at the payload region.

11.name: packed
11.about: packed_record {uint8 kind@0; uint32 seq@1; uint16 port@5; uint64 payload@7} UNALIGNED offsets + sizes. THE discrimination test: offsets must be {0,1,5,7}, never rounded/naturalized.

12.name: bitfields
12.about: bitfields packed into a single uint32 word at +0; every op is (+0, width 2/4). Must NOT fabricate a nonsense multi-offset struct; single-field struct acceptable.

13.name: runtime_index
13.about: struct row {uint32 id@0; uint32 next@4; uint64 value@16} indexed by a RUNTIME loop var. Detector must surface the constant field offsets {0,4,16} despite symbolic index scaling.

14.name: container_of
14.about: intrusive list: list_head {0,8} embedded in struct item (magic@0, link@8, name@24); owner recovered via NEGATIVE offset from the embedded member. The stable invariant is the list linkage + owner recovery; item offsets are negative/owner-relative so exact {0,8} is NOT a stable assertion here.

15.name: callback
15.about: struct session {id@0; buf@8; len@16} shared ONLY via function-pointer callbacks. No call-context edge exists; merge relies on identical type/offset bridging.

16.name: ptr_chain
16.about: struct item {id@0; next@8} through pointer-to-pointer-to-pointer. Only the leaf's +0 is ever read (no field beyond id is accessed); the invariant is that the chain does NOT fabricate garbage offsets.

17.name: by_value
17.about: struct point {x,y} passed/returned BY VALUE (register decomposition). -O0 keeps a {0,4} panel; -O2 registers may make it unobservable — the only invariant is NO nonsense multi-offset fabrication.

18.name: global_base
18.about: global_config {magic@0; version@4; flag@8; hook@16} accessed via a GLOBAL. Member loads are *(const_ptr + 0) resolved to a page-aligned global family; offsets are PAGE-RELATIVE (0x20..0x38 for the 0x404000 page). The hard invariant: ALL functions touching the same global merge into ONE candidate.

19.name: sparse_field
19.about: struct handle {pad[8]; cookie@8} — ONLY +8 is ever accessed (nonzero single offset). The pure-indirection drop (offset-0-only) MUST NOT remove it.

20.name: memcpy_noise
20.about: struct blob {magic@0; size@8; data@16} with heavy memcpy/memset noise. Noise must be skipped; real field accesses {0,8} recovered.

21.name: mutual_recursion
21.about: a_node {int32 av@0; b* bb@8} and b_node {int64 bv@0; a* aa@8} in mutual recursion. +0 accessed as BOTH 4B and 8B -> overlap may fire; must not crash or combine into nonsense.

22.name: shadow_alias
22.about: same pool[16] read as uint32[4] (+0/+4/+8/+12) AND as struct {0,8}. Different views, no declared union: detector should surface BOTH offset sets (overlap questionable — not required).

23.name: manual_iterator
23.about: struct record {key@0; value@8} walked via manual cursor advance (raw +2 per step). -O0 yields {0,8}; -O2 register walkers only leak a +0 drift so no hard offset assertion there.

24.name: wide_vector
24.about: struct pair {lo@0; hi@8} read via a single 16-byte load covering both. Adjacent narrowing must NOT fire union overlap. offsets {0,8} present.

25.name: three_level_chain
25.about: struct message {magic@0; kind@8; seq@16; payload@24} through a 3-level dispatch chain, each level touching DISJOINT fields. THE transitive-merge discriminator: ONE candidate spanning all 3 functions. (Binja renders seq/payload partially — offsets observed {0,8,0xc,0x10}; assert the merge, not the exact payload offset.)
